claims.sourceObservation: Constants declare source limit 65,536 bytes, token limit 8,192, identifier limit 64 bytes and decoded-string limit 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. lex checks source.len() before Lexer::run(false).

run dispatches ASCII space/tab/CR/LF, slash line/block comments, double-quoted strings, digit-started numbers, ASCII-letter-started words, then single-byte punctuation or unexpected_character; EOF is appended after the loop.
push refuses when existing token count is at least MAX_TOKENS-1, reserving EOF. Comments are appended to a separate collection, so they do not pass through push token counting.
Line-comment scanning ends before CR or LF, or source end. Block-comment scanning finds the first */ after its opening, with an error if absent; no nesting counter appears in this body.

Word scan starts after its first byte and accepts ASCII alphanumeric or underscore thereafter. Lexer dispatch requires initial ASCII letter; word length over 64 is refused before keyword classification.

claims.sourceObservation: Number extent includes digits, underscores and dots. validate checks a second dot first, leading-zero integer part second, integer underscore positions third, then optional nonempty fraction and its underscore positions. Underscores must have digits on both sides.
Core parse_profile and language call mori_lexer::lex, then recover token spans and decode String tokens. The inspected language body does not call first_token_text.

Lexical decimal spelling and Core UInt parsing are separate source gates: lexer validates optional fraction syntax, whereas Core literal strips underscores and calls parse::<u128>(). This statement does not report executed acceptance or rejection.

string_end tracks escaped byte state until an unescaped quote; Lexer::string calls decode_with to count emitted character len_utf8 and compares against MAX_STRING_BYTES before pushing the String token.
decode_with maps quote,backslash,slash,b,f,n,r,t escapes, uses hex4 for u escape, rejects raw characters below space, and emits other characters. hex4 reads exactly four to_digit(16) characters.

Unicode escape handling stores a pending high surrogate, combines a following low surrogate into a scalar, records the first lone surrogate while emitting replacement characters, and returns that LoneSurrogate error after the loop unless an earlier immediate error returned.

Public decode_string calls decode_with and expect("lexed strings are valid"). Its body does not return Result. first_token_text instead selects a bounded character-boundary prefix and calls run(true); run(true) stops after its first noncomment token and appends EOF.

Token stores kind and u32 start; TokenIdx wraps u16 via try_from/expect. Tokens::span calls scan::token_end, which re-scans word/number/string extents, uses zero length for EOF and one byte otherwise.

Diagnostics functions construct literal mori::lex::* codes; shown examples include source_too_large,too_many_tokens,invalid_escape,invalid_unicode_escape,lone_surrogate and division. Help-text claims are not adopted as runtime/correctness evidence.

pub fn invalid_escape(span: Span, escape: &str) -> MoriDiagnostic {
    MoriDiagnostic::error(format!("`{escape}` is not an escape I know."))
        .with_code("mori::lex::invalid_escape")
        .with_label(span.label("unknown escape"))
        .with_help_code(
            "Strings use JSON escapes. To write a backslash itself, use `\\\\`:",
            "\\\"  \\\\  \\/  \\b  \\f  \\n  \\r  \\t  \\uXXXX",
        )
}

pub fn invalid_unicode_escape(span: Span) -> MoriDiagnostic {
    MoriDiagnostic::error("A `\\u` escape needs exactly four hexadecimal digits.")
        .with_code("mori::lex::invalid_unicode_escape")
        .with_label(span.label("this escape is incomplete"))
        .with_help_code(
            "Write all four digits, or write the character directly:",
            "\"caf\\u00e9\"",
        )
}

pub fn lone_surrogate(span: Span) -> MoriDiagnostic {
    MoriDiagnostic::error("This escape is half of a surrogate pair.")
        .with_code("mori::lex::lone_surrogate")
        .with_label(span.label("this half has no partner"))
        .with_help_code(
            "A character above U+FFFF is written as a high escape followed by a low one, \

            "\"\\uD83D\\uDE00\"",
        )
